## Class III implantable device, MDD certificate under 93/42/EEC

**Class:** III (as stated)
**Route:** Article 120(3a) — certificate issued under 93/42/EEC
**Deadline:** **31 December 2027** — conditional on 120(3c)

| Question | Answer | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Which paragraph applies | 120(3a)(a) — device holds a notified-body certificate under 93/42/EEC valid by virtue of 120(2) | `[verified]` |
| Class-dependent date | 31 December 2027, the class III date (same date as class IIb implantables other than the listed exceptions) | `[verified]` |
| 3c conditions met? | **NOT ESTABLISHED** — needs confirmation from you | — |

### The important caveat

Note first that **26 May 2024 is not your market deadline**. That was the original 2017 text; Regulation (EU) 2023/607 replaced it in March 2023. If anyone in your organisation is still working to a May 2024 sunset, that is superseded.

But 26 May 2024 did not disappear — it changed job. It is now one of the dates the 2027 extension *depends on*. The extension in 120(3a) applies **only if all five** conditions in 120(3c) were met, cumulatively:

- (a) the device continues to comply with 93/42/EEC;
- (b) **no significant changes in design and intended purpose**;
- (c) no unacceptable risk to health or safety;
- (d) a **quality management system** in place under Article 10(9) **no later than 26 May 2024**;
- (e) a **formal application lodged with a notified body no later than 26 May 2024**, and a **signed written agreement with that notified body no later than 26 September 2024**.

If any of those was missed, the extension was never available to you and the answer is different — the derogation simply does not apply, and the device's position rests on the certificate's own validity, not on 2027. Can you confirm the application and written-agreement dates and the QMS?

**Also easy to miss — 120(3d):** during the transition, MDR's requirements on post-market surveillance, market surveillance, vigilance, and registration of economic operators and devices apply **in place of** the corresponding 93/42/EEC requirements. A legacy device is not living entirely under the old regime.

**What would change this:** any of the 3c conditions being unmet — most commonly the 26 May 2024 application or the 26 September 2024 written agreement. Separately, a **significant change in design or intended purpose** at any point breaks 3c(b) and ends the extension. What counts as "significant" is dealt with in MDCG guidance, which I don't have verified here — if your question turns on that, you'll need that guidance and your notified body.

## Limits

> This covers MDR Article 120(3) and (3a)–(3d) as amended by Regulation (EU) 2023/607, retrieved verbatim from the Official Journal on 2026-09-10. It does **not** cover Article 120's other paragraphs, **IVDR Article 110** (the parallel IVD transition, whose dates differ), MDCG guidance including on what counts as a significant change, Annex VII, or national practice. The transition is conditional and fact-specific; this is a first-pass aid, not legal or regulatory advice, and not a substitute for your notified body or a qualified regulatory professional.

## Short answer

**31 December 2027** — that's the last day you can *place* the device on the EU market under the MDD certificate. From 1 January 2028 you need an MDR certificate in hand.

## The legal basis

Article 120 MDR (Regulation (EU) 2017/745), as amended by **Regulation (EU) 2023/607**. The extension is risk-class-tiered:

| Device category | Placing on market until |
|---|---|
| **Class III; Class IIb implantable** (except the listed "well-established technology" items — sutures, staples, dental fillings/braces/crowns, screws, wedges, plates, wires, pins, clips, connectors) | **31 Dec 2027** |
| Other Class IIb, Class IIa, Class I with NB involvement (sterile / measuring / reusable surgical) | 31 Dec 2028 |
| Class III **custom-made** implantable | 26 May 2026 — *already passed* |

Your MDD certificate is deemed valid to that date by operation of law (Art. 120(2)) even though the date printed on it is earlier. You don't need the notified body to reissue anything.

## The conditions — check these, because the gates are in the past

The extension only applies if **all** of the following hold. Two of them had hard deadlines that expired in 2024:

1. The device continues to comply with the MDD.
2. **No significant changes** in design or intended purpose since — see MDCG 2020-3 rev.1 for what counts. This is the one that most often bites: a change you made for supply-chain or component-obsolescence reasons can silently forfeit the extension.
3. No unacceptable risk to health and safety.
4. **By 26 May 2024** you had an MDR-compliant QMS in place (Art. 10(9)).
5. **By 26 May 2024** you lodged a formal MDR conformity assessment application with a notified body, **and by 26 September 2024** you signed a written agreement with that notified body.

If 4 or 5 weren't met, the extension never applied to you and the MDD certificate lapsed on its stated expiry — you'd be placing product on the market unlawfully today. Worth confirming the signed NB agreement is on file with a date on or before 26 Sep 2024.

## Two things people commonly get wrong

**MDR obligations already apply to you.** Since 26 May 2021, the MDR rules on post-market surveillance, vigilance, registration of economic operators and devices apply to legacy devices in place of the MDD equivalents (Art. 120(3), final subparagraph). The transition period is not a pause on MDR — only on conformity assessment.

**There is no sell-off deadline any more.** Regulation 2023/607 deleted the old 26 May 2025 cut-off. Devices lawfully *placed on the market* on or before 31 Dec 2027 can continue to be made available and put into service indefinitely. So stock already in the distribution chain on 31 Dec 2027 is not stranded — the deadline constrains first placing on the market, not downstream sale.

## Practical read

You have roughly 15 months. For a Class III implantable, notified bodies are generally looking for the full technical documentation review plus clinical evaluation to be substantially complete well before the certificate date, and review cycles with deficiency rounds routinely run 12–18 months. If you're not already in active review with deficiency responses going back and forth, the 31 Dec 2027 date is at genuine risk — and there is no discretionary extension mechanism beyond Art. 59/97 national derogations, which are granted narrowly and per–Member State.

One flag: a broader targeted revision of the MDR/IVDR framework has been under discussion at Commission level. Nothing adopted changes the 2027 date, so plan against it — but it's worth having your regulatory affairs team watching that file rather than assuming the date will move.

This is a summary of the regulation as it stands, not legal advice — have your notified body confirm your specific certificate's status and your RA/legal counsel confirm the "significant changes" assessment, since that determination is device-specific and is where most challenges arise.

Web access is blocked in this session, so this is from the regulation text as I know it — verify against the current consolidated EUR-Lex version of MDR Article 120 before relying on it for a filing.

## The date: 31 December 2027

Under Article 120(2) and 120(3a)(a) of the MDR as amended by **Regulation (EU) 2023/607**, your MDD certificate is deemed valid — and the device can keep being placed on the EU market — until **31 December 2027**, because Class III is in the "higher-risk" bucket (Class III plus Class IIb implantables, excluding the listed well-established technologies like sutures, staples, dental fillings, screws, plates, wires and pins).

That's the extended date, not the certificate's printed expiry. The 2023 amendment overrides the face of the certificate.

## But it's conditional — and the gates have already closed

The extension only applies if **all** of Article 120(3c) is satisfied. Today is September 2026, so the deadlines below are in the past. These are pass/fail checks on your file, not things you can still act on:

| Condition | Deadline | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Device still complies with MDD | ongoing | — |
| No significant change in design or intended purpose | ongoing | — |
| No unacceptable risk to health/safety | ongoing | — |
| QMS per MDR Article 10(9) in place | 26 May 2024 | passed |
| Formal MDR conformity-assessment application lodged with a notified body | 26 May 2024 | passed |
| Written agreement signed with that notified body | 26 September 2024 | passed |

If any of the three dated conditions was missed, **you have no extension at all** — the legal basis for your MDD certificate lapsed on its original expiry date or on 26 May 2024, whichever applied, and continued placing on the market since then has been non-compliant. That's the first thing to confirm, ahead of any 2027 planning.

## Two things that are commonly misread

**"Placing on the market" ≠ "making available."** Regulation 2023/607 also deleted the old sell-off deadline in Article 120(4). Units you lawfully **place on the market** on or before 31 December 2027 can continue to be made available down the distribution chain and put into service **with no end date**. So stock in distributors' hands on 1 January 2028 is not stranded. What stops on 31 December 2027 is your ability to place *new* units on the market without an MDR certificate.

**MDR obligations already apply to you now.** Article 120(3) substitutes the MDR requirements for post-market surveillance, market surveillance, vigilance, and registration of economic operators and devices in place of the MDD ones. You are a legacy device, not an MDD-only device. Also note Article 10a (from Regulation (EU) 2024/1860), in force since 10 January 2025: you must give advance notice to competent authorities and economic operators if you're going to interrupt or discontinue supply — which bites directly if you decide not to pursue MDR certification for this device.

**No significant change** is the condition most likely to trip you up over the next 15 months. Design changes, intended-purpose changes, and certain supplier/manufacturing changes can void the extension. MDCG 2020-3 rev.1 is the guidance to work against before you approve any change to this device.

## What "fully MDR certified" needs to mean in practice

Aim to hold the MDR certificate in hand well before 31 December 2027, not on it. Notified body capacity for Class III implantables is the binding constraint, and review cycles including non-conformity rounds routinely run past 12–18 months. If your NB hasn't yet completed the design dossier review, get a dated milestone plan from them now.

If certification is going to slip past the date, the fallback routes are Article 59(1) (competent-authority derogation, national, per-country) or Article 97(1) — both are exceptional, discretionary, and not a plan.

**Suggested next step:** pull the file and confirm the three 2024 dates were met, with documentary evidence of the signed NB agreement in particular. Tell me what you find and I can work through the implications from there.

## Short answer

**31 December 2027** — but only if you met a set of conditions whose deadlines were in 2024. There is no extension beyond that date for Class III, and no further sell-off cliff after it.

## Where the date comes from

Article 120 MDR ((EU) 2017/745), as amended by **Regulation (EU) 2023/607**. MDD certificates that (a) were issued before 26 May 2021 and (b) were still valid on 20 March 2023 and have not since been withdrawn remain valid until:

| Device class | Transitional end date |
|---|---|
| Class III; Class IIb implantable (except the "well-established technology" list — sutures, staples, dental fillings, braces, crowns, screws, wedges, plates, wires, pins, clips, connectors) | **31 Dec 2027** |
| Other Class IIb, Class IIa, Class I sterile / measuring / reusable surgical | 31 Dec 2028 |

A Class III implantable falls squarely in the first row. The WET carve-out doesn't help you — it only applies to Class IIb implantables.

Two things worth knowing about the mechanics:

- The extension operates **by law**, not by re-issued certificate. If your certificate's printed expiry has already passed, that is fine; it is still valid for MDR purposes. Notified bodies issue confirmation letters for customers and customs, and that's usually what tenders ask for.
- The **sell-off deadline was deleted** entirely by 2023/607 (old Art. 120(4) is gone). Units you lawfully *place on the market* on or before 31 Dec 2027 can continue to be made available and put into service after that date with no end date. The 2027 cliff is on placing on the market — first supply of each individual unit in the EU — not on distributors' or hospitals' existing stock.

## The conditions — this is the part that actually matters now

The extension was never automatic. Under Article 120(3c) you needed, cumulatively:

1. Continued compliance with the MDD.
2. **No significant changes** in design or intended purpose.
3. No unacceptable risk to health and safety.
4. An **MDR-compliant QMS in place by 26 May 2024**.
5. A **formal MDR conformity assessment application lodged with a notified body by 26 May 2024** (Annex VII 4.3, first paragraph) — for this device or its replacement.
6. A **written agreement signed with that notified body by 26 September 2024** (Annex VII 4.3, second paragraph).

All three dated conditions are ~2 years in the past. So the real question isn't "how long do we have" — it's **which of these you can evidence**. If items 4–6 were met, you're covered to 31 Dec 2027. If the application or the signed agreement was missed, the extension never attached to this device, and it has not been lawfully placeable on the EU market since — that's a live compliance exposure now, not a 2027 problem. That's the first thing I'd go verify, and I'd want to see the dated application acknowledgement and the countersigned NB agreement, not just an internal assertion that it was handled.

Also note that since 26 May 2021 the MDR chapters on post-market surveillance, market surveillance, vigilance, and registration of economic operators and devices have applied to your legacy device in place of the MDD equivalents, and surveillance of the device sits with your MDR notified body under that signed agreement — not with your old MDD notified body.

## Planning back from 31 Dec 2027

To keep placing product after that date you need the **MDR certificate issued** — not merely submitted, not "in final review" — by 31 Dec 2027. For a Class III implantable that means Annex IX full QMS plus design dossier examination, and for an implantable also the Article 54 clinical evaluation consultation procedure (expert panel) if it's in a relevant category. Notified body review cycles for Class III design dossiers have been running long, with multiple deficiency rounds normal. From September 2026 that is roughly 15 months of calendar for a process that commonly takes longer, so if your dossier isn't already deep into review the schedule risk is real.

If you're going to miss it, the fallbacks are national and discretionary, not a strategy: an Article 59 derogation from a competent authority (single-market-wide only if the Commission extends it), or forbearance via the Article 97 non-compliance route. Both are country-by-country and neither is something to plan around.

## The caveat on my date

As of May 2026, **no further extension of 31 December 2027 had been adopted**. The Commission had signalled a broader MDR/IVDR revision with a legislative proposal expected around end-2026, and there was industry pressure over Class III/IIb capacity — but a proposal is years from applying, and nothing in it had changed Article 120. Given the date sensitivity here, confirm against the consolidated Article 120 on EUR-Lex and the current MDCG guidance before you act on the 2027 date. If you re-enable web access I'll check that directly.

I'm giving you the regulatory reading, not legal advice — for a Class III implantable with a possible gap in the 120(3c) conditions, get your regulatory counsel and your notified body on it.
